Exchanger approach is 8.4 C above its clean baseline despite independently confirmed near-commanded flow. Adequate inlet pressure and absent cavitation-frequency vibration argue against pump cavitation. The bypass is confirmed closed, temperature sensors agree, and current load is steady below design maximum. Together these findings strongly favor exchanger fouling.

The exchanger heat-transfer coefficient is 39% below its clean reference at matched flow, its approach temperature is elevated, and cleaning is overdue. Sensors agree, flow is near command, inlet pressure is adequate, and independent indication confirms the bypass is closed. Persistence across stable loads argues against a transient.

The exchanger approach is 8.4 C above its clean baseline despite near-commanded flow, supporting degraded exchanger heat transfer. Stable inlet pressure above the cavitation margin and normal motor current weaken pump cavitation. Independent confirmation of a closed bypass, agreement between temperature sensors, and steady sub-design load weaken the other alternatives. Fouling remains unconfirmed by a controlled performance test.

The heat-transfer coefficient is 39% below the clean reference at matched flow, and the hot-side approach is 8.4 C above baseline, strongly supporting fouling. Independent position verification confirms the bypass is closed; temperature sensors agree, flow is near command, and load is steady. Adequate inlet pressure argues against cavitation; the uncorroborated pump hum provides only weak contrary evidence.

Exchanger approach is 8.4 C above its clean baseline despite near-commanded flow, normal inlet temperature, and steady below-design load, strongly favoring fouling. Adequate pump inlet pressure, independently confirmed bypass closure, and agreement between temperature sensors weaken the competing fault diagnoses. A transient remains possible because only current operating conditions were checked.

The supplied reports consistently favor fouling, with the stronger reports incorporating a controlled test showing heat-transfer performance 39% below the clean reference. The newly acquired borescope inspection directly confirms widespread mineral deposition narrowing multiple exchanger channels, resolving their main verification gap. The reported pump hum is weak contrary evidence relative to the thermal and physical findings.

The reports share evidence and should not be treated as independent confirmations; the direct inspection provides the decisive additional support.
